_comment: Process files in `order` with one shared dedupe set, then the OpenCode database, then the Antigravity databases in `antigravity.order` (same dedupe set). Paths are relative to this folder. `mtimes` (Unix ms) give the modification times that produce both orders; apply them to a copy of this folder before computing daily history. `traces` (Gemini, omp) give the phase after feeding a file up to and including physical line `afterLine` (after the files before it in `order`). omp: the folder `omp` plays ~/.omp, so its automatic roots are omp/agent/sessions and omp/profiles/*/agent/sessions; `omp.discover` lists what discovery finds there. Antigravity: the folder `antigravity` plays ~/.gemini (stores antigravity-cli, antigravity, antigravity-ide); each database is one agent whose id is its path; `{"unsupported": true}` marks a database that contributes no agent; reading must not create any file (no -wal or -shm). WorkBuddy: the folder `workbuddy` plays the home folder (data folders .workbuddy and .workbuddy-ai); `workbuddy.discover` lists what discovery finds in both projects folders; its `traces` work like the omp ones. Pi: the folder `pi` plays ~/.pi with this folder as home (pi/agent/settings.json names the custom session folder ~/pi/custom-sessions); `pi.discover` lists what discovery finds in both roots; its `traces` work like the omp ones. OpenClaw: the folder `openclaw` plays the home folder (state folders .openclaw and the profile .openclaw-work); after the OpenCode and Antigravity databases, the agent databases of `openclaw.dbOrder` are read with the same dedupe set, each one agent per transcript window (agent id `<database>#<session id>`, relative to this folder); `{"unsupported": true}` marks a database without session tables; `openclaw.discover` lists the databases discovery finds, `openclaw.codexDiscover` the rollouts of the Codex roots next to them (METRICS 2); a trace gives the phase of a window after its row `afterSeq`, after the databases before it; reading must not create any file. Hermes Agent: see `hermes._comment`; its log files are not in `order` (one parser state per log folder) but their modification times are in `mtimes`. Factory Droid: see `droid._comment`; its transcripts are in `order` (each read with its sidecar, whose modification time is in `mtimes` too) and its `traces` work like the omp ones. Every agent's `effort` and `speed` are the current values of EXECUTION-MODES, so they follow the files the fixture folders play: codex/config.toml, gemini/settings.json, antigravity/config/config.json, workbuddy/*/workbuddy.db and settings.json, and hermes/home's state.db and config.yaml; `responseModes` never depends on them.

hermes._comment: Hermes Agent (METRICS 4.15). `home` plays the Hermes home; `discover` lists the log files of its log folders. Feed the files of `order` (modification times `mtimes`) to one parser state per log folder, with wall times in `timeZone`, and the shared dedupe set; `sets` gives, per log folder, its malformed API-call lines and one agent per session id (the empty id is the agent of lines without a session tag; agent id = absolute folder path + '#' + id), in the order agents first appear. `traces` give one session's phase after feeding a file up to and including physical line `afterLine`, after the files before it in `order`. `wallTimes` convert a record line's timestamp in a zone (null: not a record line). `homes` resolve the Hermes home from an environment. `rotation` replays a log folder with real renames: `append` writes `lines` (each followed by a newline) or raw `text` to a file and sets its modification time, `rename` and `delete` change files, `read` reads every file of the folder from the offset its identity reached and checks every response key emitted so far and the listed agents. `runtimeConfigs` give config.yaml texts and whether they select the Codex runtime; `agentConfigs` give texts and the two scalars of their `agent` block (EXECUTION-MODES). `home` also holds `state.db`, whose sessions give the agents' session-current effort. `codexRuntime` replays a Hermes home (folder `home`, with the profile `p`): `write` sets a file's text (`size`: padded with `#` to that many bytes) and modification time, `remove` deletes it, `append` works like the rotation's, and `read` checks the config.yaml of every log folder, then reads its new lines, and checks each listed log folder's switch, every response key emitted so far and the listed agents.

droid._comment: Factory Droid (METRICS 4.16). The folder `droid` plays the home folder; `discover` lists the sessions discovery finds under droid/.factory/sessions. Its sessions are in `order` and `files` (each read from the start: the history rule); the history analysis also emits the own counters of a session without calls (I) as `droid:<session id>:session`. `roots`: create the folders `make` in a scratch folder, resolve the setting (null: the automatic root of the scratch folder as home) and compare with `expected` (relative). `sidecars`: a sidecar's text (`size`: padded with spaces to that many bytes) and whether it is readable, its counters and session model (`encoding`: the text's bytes in that encoding instead of UTF-8). `allocations`: the largest-remainder split of `total` by `weights`. `live`: scripted read cycles in a scratch home (see its _comment). `history`: scripted history analyses in a scratch home (see its _comment).

sidecars.name: blank pick falls back to the model

live._comment: Steps, in order, in a scratch home: `append` writes `lines` (each followed by \n) to a transcript; `rewrite` replaces it with `lines` through a new file (a new identity); `sidecar` writes the transcript's sidecar (`doc` as JSON) and sets its modification time (ms); `open` starts following a transcript (`atEnd`: it starts at its end, older than the startup window); a `sidecar` step with `text` writes that text instead of `doc`; `read` runs one read cycle of that transcript and compares every response emitted so far (the latest version of each key, in first-emission order), the growth still waiting (P) and, when given, the phase.

history._comment: Steps in a scratch home with only Factory Droid sessions: `write` sets a file's `text` and modification time (ms); `analyze` runs a history analysis of the home's sessions (METRICS 8, the history rule of 4.16), keeping the remembered parent signatures from the analyses before, and compares the responses per session file and the session files skipped because their own counters are unknown.
